findings.description: The trigger says execution is longer than the configured limit, but detection is required when the limit expires. At expiry the execution time equals the limit, so the boundary and detection instant are ambiguous. CON-SUP-103 uses both formulations.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the boundary condition and detection instant with the product owner, and state a consistent rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires the checkpoint of every task released in a control cycle by that cycle's end, while CON-SUP-103 permits T_DIAG to execute for up to 20 ms in a 10 ms control cycle. The checkpoint's position within task execution is unspecified, so a permitted T_DIAG execution may be treated as a flow fault.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the checkpoint timing and cycle rule for T_DIAG with the product owner, then state a consistent, testable condition.

findings.description: The requirement permits watchdog refresh only while every supervised task is healthy, but neither the item nor its cited sources defines when a task is considered healthy, including before its first completion or after a detected fault.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable health condition governing refresh, including startup and fault behavior, using an agreed source.

findings.description: The requirement permits watchdog refresh only while every supervised task is healthy, but neither the item nor its cited sources defines when a task is considered healthy, including before its first completion or after a detected fault.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable health condition governing refresh, including startup and fault behavior, using an agreed source.

findings.description: The requirement specifies a CRC-32 check of the application image, but CON-SUP-107 specifies a stored CRC-32 only for the configuration block; it does not specify the application-image check algorithm or its reference value.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and record the agreed application-image integrity method and reference data, or remove the unsupported CRC-32 specification and record the missing decision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies a CRC-32 polynomial, but neither it nor the requirement specifies the other parameters needed to reproduce the stored CRC, such as initialization, reflection and final XOR. A verifier cannot determine a unique expected result.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and reference a complete CRC definition, including its parameters and configuration-block coverage.

findings.description: The requirement directs the status signal high whenever startup checks have passed and no fault is present. CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-027 require the safe state to remain latched until power-on after repeated faults, including across software and watchdog resets.
findings.requested_change: Include the safe-state latch in the conditions governing the operational status signal.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires a fault report within 10 ms of detection, while CON-SUP-110 requires transmission after entering the safe state and SYS-SUP-022 and SYS-SUP-023 allow up to 50 ms to reach it. The required ordering and deadlines can conflict; the item also independently requires transmission after safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the report ordering and deadlines with the product owner, and state mutually achievable conditions.

findings.description: The item treats every watchdog reset as a detected fault. SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023 and SYS-SUP-042 then require a safe-state reaction and supervisor reset, potentially causing repeated resets after a watchdog reset. CON-SUP-111 requires classification and CON-SUP-112 names code 8, but neither specifies this recovery loop.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the intended reporting and recovery behavior for a watchdog reset with the product owner, and specify how it interacts with the fault reaction.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 defines the timestamp as milliseconds since start without identifying the start reference; OP-SYS-001 records this uncertainty. The allowed entity values also do not identify an appropriate entity for watchdog reset code 8.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the timestamp reference and the entity value for watchdog reset reports.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 and the requirement name the response field <state> but do not define its possible values or their meanings. A verifier cannot determine the correct status response.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the permitted state values and their mapping to controller states.

findings.description: The requirement says to return the last 8 fault reports but does not specify the response when fewer than eight faults are retained. CON-SUP-113 also leaves this case unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the response for fewer than eight retained reports, including an empty history.

findings.description: The requirement unconditionally requests a software reset after entering the safe state, whereas STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 require the controller to remain in the safe state until power-on when the repeated-fault latch applies. CON-SUP-115 also requires a configuration fault to latch the safe state.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset request conditions and exceptions consistently with the agreed safe-state latch behavior.
